target_customer: Homes, small businesses and public hotspot users in dense African cities, starting with Lagos
problem: Fixed broadband was scarce and expensive in urban Nigeria, and grid power was unreliable for network equipment.
business_model: Consumer and business ISP subscriptions on owned solar-powered Wi-Fi towers, under the Wifi.com.ng brand

founders.name: Kendall Ananyi
education: Master's in computer engineering (per company site)
founders.background_notes: Company site says over 19 years in telecoms and software.

founders.name: Ifeanyi Okonkwo
founders.background_notes: YC page: worked on the team that launched BlackBerry in Nigeria and expanded to Ghana.

competitors.name: Spectranet
competitors.traction_then: 193,892 of 390,794 corporate and SME subscribers in NCC data for November 2017

competitors.name: Smile Communications
competitors.traction_then: 156,243 customers in NCC data for November 2017

technical_complexity.rationale: Building and operating a network of solar-powered Wi-Fi towers needs RF engineering and field operations, not research-grade work.

defensibility.rationale: Owned towers and installed base are capital-heavy to replicate, but wireless ISPs and telcos compete for the same customers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought it; Tizeti remained independent, partnered with Facebook on Express Wi-Fi in November 2017 and with Microsoft in Cote d'Ivoire per a TechCabal tag page.

market_need_then: Nigeria had 37 active ISPs in November 2017 yet dominated by two players, per an industry map. Tizeti reported 7,000 hotspots and 150,000 users by September 2018.

branding.domain_note: Consumer brand uses Wifi.com.ng, a descriptive local-domain brand; also GhanaWiFi and Tizeti BBN brands.
branding.brand_signature: Unlimited plan at 30 dollars per month and Comcast for Africa positioning per ImpactAlpha

brand_strength.rationale: A descriptive consumer brand, Wifi.com.ng, was widely used for hotspots and covered over 70 percent of Lagos per the company, while the corporate name Tizeti is distinctive but unexplained.

outcome_analysis: Tizeti raised a 2.1 million dollar seed in 2017 and a 3 million dollar Series A in September 2018 led by 4DX Ventures, then expanded into Ghana and Cote d'Ivoire. It stayed independent. A 2020 harassment probe cleared the CEO and he returned. Later subscriber counts are far below Spectranet, so it grew modestly rather than dominating.
notes: Series A stated by the company and ImpactAlpha, plus many outlets in search results. Seed amount from the company release, ImpactAlpha says raised last July (likely July 2017). Competitors are cited from a June 2018 industry map reporting November 2017 NCC data, about eight months after the batch start; treat as approximate. Founding year conflicts: Wikipedia 2017, one source says Wifi.com.ng launched 2014; so null. Walter Baddoo of 4DX joined the board as an investor, not a founder. Q4 2023 subscriber comparison noted in search results only.
